The **Epstein list** is a hypothesized document containing the names of high-profile clients to whom the American financier and convicted child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein allegedly trafficked young girls, part of the wider body of documents known as the **Epstein files**.

Epstein cultivated a social circle of public figures that included politicians and celebrities, fueling conspiracy theories suggesting that he maintained such a list to blackmail these associates—and that his 2019 death was not a suicide (as officially reported) but a murder to protect his clients.

The petition's final two signatures were to come from Democrats: James Walkinshaw after he won the Virginia 11th District special election on September 9[158] and Adelita Grijalva (expected) after she won the Arizona 7th congressional district special election on September 23.[159] Though Walkinshaw was sworn in the day after the election, Grijalva was treated differently.

House Speaker Mike Johnson said he would wait until the state certified her victory.[160] He then canceled the House sessions for the last two days of September while facing an impending government shutdown[161] and said he would not call the House back into session until the government was operating again.[162][163] On October 14, the Arizona Secretary of State certified the election result.[164] On October 21, Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes sued Johnson, seeking to force him to swear in Grijalva.[165] That day, Johnson told Fox Business that the delay "has zero to do with Epstein", given that "the Epstein files are being released.
There's 43,000 pages now out there".[166] That number apparently referred mainly to the House Oversight Committee's releases on September 2 and October 17.
